# Interaction Requirements Checklist: Site Interaction Affordances

**Purpose**: Review the completeness, clarity, consistency, and measurability of the footer, documentation-navigation, and theme-control requirements
**Created**: 2026-09-08
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `$speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

## Requirement Completeness

- [ ] CHK001 Are all six existing footer destinations assigned an explicit browsing-context policy? [Completeness, Spec §FR-001 through FR-005]
- [ ] CHK002 Are opener isolation and referrer disclosure requirements defined for every approved separate-context destination? [Completeness, Spec §FR-003]
- [ ] CHK003 Are pagination requirements defined for both direction cues, wrapped labels, single-card pages, and two-card pages? [Coverage, Spec §FR-007 through FR-009]
- [ ] CHK004 Are enabled, selected, and disabled theme-control states all addressed independently? [Completeness, Spec §FR-010 through FR-013]

## Requirement Clarity

- [ ] CHK005 Is the exact separate-context destination set unambiguous despite Company's different hostname? [Clarity, Spec §FR-002 through FR-005]
- [ ] CHK006 Is the one-pixel center-alignment tolerance defined against the complete label group rather than a single text line? [Clarity, Spec §FR-007]
- [ ] CHK007 Is stable chevron sizing specific enough to prohibit shrinking without prescribing an arbitrary visual redesign? [Clarity, Spec §FR-009]
- [ ] CHK008 Is pointer treatment tied to actual enabled state rather than current-theme selection? [Clarity, Spec §FR-010 through FR-012]

## Requirement Consistency

- [ ] CHK009 Do footer behavior requirements agree across user scenarios, functional requirements, assumptions, and scope boundaries? [Consistency, Spec §US1, FR-001 through FR-006]
- [ ] CHK010 Do pointer-cursor requirements preserve selected and disabled semantics without making cursor shape the only state cue? [Consistency, Spec §FR-010 through FR-013]
- [ ] CHK011 Do responsive alignment requirements preserve the existing layout while requiring consistent internal cue placement? [Consistency, Spec §FR-006 through FR-009]

## Acceptance Criteria Quality

- [ ] CHK012 Can the footer behavior contract be objectively evaluated by destination label, browsing context, and relationship policy? [Measurability, Spec §SC-001 and SC-002]
- [ ] CHK013 Can pagination alignment be objectively evaluated across every required route class and width? [Measurability, Spec §SC-003]
- [ ] CHK014 Can theme-control cursor and semantic-state outcomes be evaluated independently for enabled and disabled controls? [Measurability, Spec §SC-004 and SC-005]

## Scenario and Edge-Case Coverage

- [ ] CHK015 Are keyboard, focus, pointer, touch-target, reduced-motion, and both-theme requirements specified for all affected controls? [Coverage, Spec §FR-013 through FR-017]
- [ ] CHK016 Are future external-looking destinations explicitly prevented from inheriting behavior through hostname inference? [Edge Case, Spec §Edge Cases]
- [ ] CHK017 Are first-page, interior-page, and last-page pagination shapes included in the required coverage? [Coverage, Spec §FR-016]
- [ ] CHK018 Are negative requirements defined for each known regression class without weakening the full publication gate? [Coverage, Spec §SC-007 and SC-008]

## Notes

- Mark items `[x]` only after review confirms the requirement-quality criterion is satisfied.
- Leave items unchecked when they still require clarification, correction, or reviewer evaluation.
- `$speckit-implement` reads checklist checkbox state as a gate and must not modify markers.
- `checklists/requirements.md` has a separate built-in lifecycle maintained by `$speckit-specify` and `$speckit-clarify`.
- Add comments or findings inline.
